messages:
Carmen S.: Customer on Dedicated/VPC reporting intermittent SSO failures. They see 302 -> our callback but the app logs show no Authorization header. Works against Hosted, fails only through their LB + our ingress. Repro steps attached from customer.

Alice M.: can you paste the minimal repro curl they used?

Carmen S.: sure. Customer curl to the public ALB: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJ..." https://private-cust.example.com/_auth/callback
```
They say ALB TLS terminates, then traffic goes ALB -> NLB -> istio-ingress -> app. ALB access logs show Authorization, app headers do not.

Ben T.: classic multi-proxy header loss. Could be ALB stripping, NLB/proxy protocol conversion, or an Envoy/Istio filter. Also watch for `proxy_set_header` omissions in custom nginx.

customer-ops: pasted sanitized logs: 
```
ALB log: request_headers:{"Authorization":"Bearer ..."}
app dump: headers: {"host":"private-cust.example.com", "x-forwarded-for":"10.1.2.3"}
```
So ALB shows header, app doesn't receive it.

Dave R.: can you tcpdump on the ingress node to confirm header is on the wire to the pod? That will prove where it's removed.

Carmen S.: tcpdump on node shows the full HTTP/1.1 request with Authorization present when arriving at the node: 
```
GET /_auth/callback HTTP/1.1
Host: private-cust.example.com
Authorization: Bearer ...
...
```
But the pod still logs no Authorization.

Ben T.: then it's our sidechain (Envoy/Istio plugin) that strips it. Grep for EnvoyFilters or Gateways that touch headers. Commands I ran previously: 
```
kubectl -n istio-system get envoyfilter -o yaml | sed -n '1,200p'
kubectl -n customer-ns get gateway -o yaml
```
Look for header_operations with remove.

Carmen S.: did that, found this in an EnvoyFilter created by the partner onboarding job (owner: partner-onboarding helm chart): 
```
patch: 
  - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER
    match: { context: GATEWAY }
    patch: 
      operation: MERGE
      value:
        typed_config:
          '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.header_to_metadata.v3.Config
          request_rules:
            - header: Authorization
              remove: true
```
So the filter explicitly removes Authorization.

Alice M.: wow, partner onboarding added a global remove rule. That explains intermittent breakage for tenants behind that routing. We should not have global header scrubs.

Dave R.: immediate mitigation options:
- patch EnvoyFilter to limit match to partner path or specific ingress namespace
- replace `remove` with a conditional that only strips for requests matching the partner WAF behavior
- or add a `set_request_headers` action to copy `x-forwarded-authorization` (if ALB rewrites to that) back into `authorization`

Carmen S.: I patched the EnvoyFilter in staging to scope the rule to `prefix: "/partner/"` and applied to the customer cluster. Then rolled the istio-ingressgateway pods.

deploy-bot: rolling restart started for deployment/istio-ingressgateway (3 pods)

Carmen S.: after the restart, customer retried the SSO flow and reported success — Authorization header present and callback flows completed. They confirmed no more 401s.

Ben T.: follow-ups: search all clusters for similar filters and for helm charts that apply global header operations. Run: 
```
kubectl get clusters --all-namespaces -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}'
# then for each do: kubectl get envoyfilter --all-namespaces -o yaml | grep -i remove
```
Also add a CI/qa check that prevents global `remove: ["authorization"]` patches.

Alice M.: also update partner onboarding docs and the helm chart to scope header scrubs. Notify partner that their default config is unsafe for tenant traffic.

Dave R.: I'll create an infra ticket TICK-8891 to: 1) audit EnvoyFilters in prod, 2) add an alert to detect header mismatches (correlate LB logs and app logs via request-id), 3) add an end-to-end integration test asserting Authorization is forwarded through ingress for Dedicated tenants.

Carmen S.: filing internal postmortem and attaching repro curl and the patched EnvoyFilter yaml to the ticket. Will also share a minimal reproducer: cURL -> ALB -> NLB-ish -> istio-ingress with a header scrub rule.

partner-bot: note: partner-onboarding v2.3.1 removed global header scrub in default values. Users should upgrade.

Alice M.: good triage everyone. Closing thread here, will track work in TICK-8891.

Carmen S.: closing — thanks all :white_check_mark:
